solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knock journalist Spooner says is a beast

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words before his name get their starts exchanged

blocks.note: a knock is a bump, whose opening sound is swapped with the next word's
a hack is a jobbing journalist, and it takes the other word's opening sound

explanation.surface: Someone thumps a reporter and is called an animal for it.
explanation.walkthrough: BUMP HACK with its first sounds swapped becomes HUMP BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The humpback is a large whale, an animal of the ocean.

clue.text: Sweet smell … cheese off?

blocks.note: in British slang a hum is a bad smell
to cheese off is British slang for to annoy, and so is to bug

explanation.surface: A sweet that smells like cheese gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese off' looks like cheese going rotten, but it is a phrasal verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a hard, striped British boiled candy, often mint flavoured.

clue.text: Fashion item old lady and knight chat about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for chat runs backwards

blocks.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma
N is the chess notation for the knight
gab is idle chat

explanation.surface: An elderly woman and a knight gossip about the latest accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-bag is a small shoulder bag carried by men, a trendy accessory.

clue.text: Place to get a bite from fish around river by lake

indicators.note: around says the fish word surrounds the river letter

blocks.note: the bass is a fish
R is the standard abbreviation for river
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Where an angler might get a bite from a fish near a river and lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bite' suggests a fish taking the bait; it is a quick meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant, where you go to eat a snack or meal.

clue.text: The old cedar building is detached and remote

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so these letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aged wooden building stands alone and far off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold-hearted person lacks warmth and feeling, aloof and unsympathetic towards others.

clue.text: Relies on support, having caught touch of tonsillitis

indicators.note: a mere touch of something is just its first bit, so only the opening letter is wanted
having caught says the support word holds the other letter inside it

blocks.note: a truss is a supporting framework or surgical support
the opening letter of the illness

explanation.surface: A patient with a sore throat leans on a support.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust someone is to depend on them, so trusts means depends upon.

clue.text: Mature with no time for nonsense? Essentially responsible!

indicators.note: with no time says the letter for time is removed from the word for nonsense
the essence of a word is its very centre, so only its middle letter is kept

blocks.note: tripe is rubbish or nonsense
T is the abbreviation for time
the sixth of eleven letters sits in the middle

explanation.surface: Grown-ups have no time for silliness; they are responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to develop fully or come of age, as fruit does.

clue.text: Petition to stop substanceless Swiss graffiti artists

indicators.note: without its substance a word keeps only its outside letters
to stop something is to plug it, so the petition word fills the gap

blocks.note: a prayer is a petition or request
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A petition is raised to halt vandals in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is usually applied with aerosol paint cans, so its artists spray their work.

clue.text: Conservative in strappy wear creates uproars

indicators.note: in places the party letter inside the footwear word

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
sandals are open shoes held on by straps

explanation.surface: A Tory politician turns up in strappy shoes and causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals provoke public outrage and commotion, which is what uproars are.

clue.text: Geezers add up numbers using their minds

blocks.note: geezer is British slang for a man
to tally is to count up

explanation.surface: Blokes do sums in their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mentally means doing it in the head, with thought alone and no aids.

clue.text: Greek city corners recalled Athens at first

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs in the opposite direction
at first keeps just the opening letter of the city name

blocks.note: to corner someone is to trap them
its first letter

explanation.surface: A historian recalls how Athens cornered an enemy early in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corners' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in traps an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the ancient warrior city-state of the Peloponnese, Athens' great rival.

clue.text: Range of exams not initially offered by uni

indicators.note: not initially says the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
orals are spoken examinations

explanation.surface: A university fails to offer a full set of spoken exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offered by' places the university letter before what remains of the exams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are the mountain chain dividing Europe from Asia in Russia.

clue.text: Chestnutty horse of French revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the French word is spun backwards

blocks.note: a hackney is a breed of carriage horse
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse belongs to a French rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnutty' suggests a horse's colour; an old chestnut is a stale joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is an overused joke, so something chestnutty is stale and overworn.

clue.text: Old statesman in March able to enter foreign state

indicators.note: being put into a foreign state means the letters become unfamiliar, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician gets a chance in spring to visit another country.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain was British Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain was a British prime minister and politician of the past, hence an old statesman.

clue.text: Officer finally involved in a dire alarm at sea?

definitions.text: Officer finally involved in a dire alarm at sea?

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval officer is caught up in a terrible emergency on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a senior naval officer who might be caught up in a crisis on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear admiral is a senior naval rank, an officer who serves aboard ships.

clue.text: Marmoset roaming around Lima is a danger in the main

indicators.note: something roaming wanders about, so the animal's letters move into a new order
around says the rearranged letters wrap the code letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A monkey loose in the Peruvian capital is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a hazard to ships on the ocean.

clue.text: Small vegetable magnate giving a lecture?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the pea is a vegetable
a magnate is a business king, as in an oil king

explanation.surface: A minor vegetable tycoon delivers a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecturing involves talking to an audience, so a lecturer is addressing listeners aloud.

clue.text: I’m a little stirrer!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone owning up to being a mischief-maker who likes causing trouble
setter's reading: a small utensil for mixing a hot drink in a cup

explanation.walkthrough: A stirrer is British slang for someone who stirs up trouble; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The small spoon is used for stirring sugar into tea or coffee.

clue.text: Earnest pleb must get changed to appear thus

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that thus stands for: how one must look

indicators.note: getting changed means altering, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A serious commoner has to put on different clothes to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get changed' suggests changing clothes; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presentable means smart enough to be seen in public, fit for company.

clue.text: Wander off track with record-holder Bolt?

indicators.note: a holder contains something, so the bolt word holds the record word

blocks.note: a dart is a bolt or arrow; to dart is also to bolt
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, the sprint record-holder, runs off the track.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt holds the 100m world record, but here bolt is just a dart.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart from a path is to deviate or stray away from it.

clue.text: Go to see a nurse, with temperature taken

indicators.note: taken means taken in, so the temperature letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A visit to a nurse who takes your temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event or appointment means to be present there, to go along.

clue.text: Escapee a rubbish criminal communist turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for communist reads backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
BS is a slang abbreviation for nonsense
a con is a convict
red is a standard word for a communist

explanation.surface: A runaway: a hopeless crook and a communist who changed sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An absconder runs away secretly, typically from custody, making them a fugitive.

clue.text: More daring to go topless in one’s later years

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: bolder means braver

explanation.surface: Someone becomes braver about going topless as they age.
explanation.definitionFit: Older describes greater age, being further along in life than before.

clue.text: Track broadcast on radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are only heard, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: broadcast means transmitted or dispatched

explanation.surface: A song track is played over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a piece of music; it is the trail a hound follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is the trail of smell left by an animal, which hounds follow.

clue.text: Legendary royal drug-dealer’s confession?

blocks.note: what a dealer might admit: I sold
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer owns up to selling ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession is 'I sold E', ecstasy being the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan and Isolde legend.

clue.text: One engaged in motor madness in coach

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the numeral sits inside the phrase

blocks.note: motor is CAR and madness is RAGE
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A passenger gets caught up in road fury on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a bus; it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a railway passenger car, or a horse-drawn vehicle, both carriages.

clue.text: Dope experiment produces pretty high people

blocks.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: Testing drugs makes people very high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'high' suggest drugs; dope is inside information here.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class just below the nobility, fairly elevated in social rank.

clue.text: A flipping awful noise? Pal’s stuck in chipper!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the noise word runs backwards
stuck in says the friend word is inserted into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a din is a loud racket
mate is British for friend

explanation.surface: A furious complaint about a racket from a mate inside a chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive; 'chipper' suggests an Irish chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means cheerful and lively, so a chipper person is lively and spirited.
